append.text: **Ps 43:14 (D39's open question ruled): *derísum* kept apart → *riso*** (*zombaria e riso*): 78:4 is the near-twin that varies exactly this word, and the Greek varies it too (καταγέλως vs χλευασμός); *riso* is the root of de-rídeo and κατα-γέλως. No reader remarked. See the derísum row.

**Ps 43:4b *e a luz do vosso rosto*:** the row held — the Latinist asked *iluminação* twice (minor), refused (26:1; heard as lighting); option kept in Ps 43's decision `illuminatio`. 89:8 will meet the same request.

**Ps 43:13 *e não houve multidão nas trocas deles*:** the Latin's openness (a great sum, or a crowd of buyers) kept; the blind reader found no clear meaning; options *abundância*, *concorrência* (MS1932).
**Ps 43:22 *os segredos do coração*** — as foreseen; no reader remarked.
**Ps 43:22b (= Rom 8:36) *somos entregues à morte o dia todo*** — the passive (MS1932); *somos mortos* (DRB) is heard 'dead'; option.
**Ps 43:23 *por que adormeceis, Senhor?*** — applied; no reader remarked.

**Ps 43:10 the plural of the people's hosts *in virtútibus nostris* → *com as nossas forças*** (v2): draft 1 *poderes* was heard abstract by the blind reader, and the Latinist and the stylist asked *forças* independently. See the row *virtútes nostræ*.
**Ps 43:24 *esqueceis a nossa carência*** — the noun of D38's *carente*; the stylist wanted *pobreza* (pauper's), refused.

terms: | derísum | riso (*zombaria e riso para os que estão ao nosso redor*) | open | Ps 43:14 (καταγέλως); rules D39's question: kept apart from illúsio → *escárnio* (78:4, the near-twin, has illúsio, and the Greek differs too). Options *escárnio*, *irrisão*, *chacota*. Cost: *escarnecer* (derídere, 21:8) is another family in Portuguese. |

| virtútes nostræ (plural, the people's hosts) | forças (*e não saireis, Deus, com as nossas forças*) | open | Ps 43:10; **59:12b and 107:12b are the same colon and should copy it**. Holds strength and armed forces as the Latin plural does; *exércitos* (DRB, MS1932) decides. The singular virtus stays *poder*, *Dóminus virtútum* *Senhor dos poderes*; cost: *fortitúdo → força* (17:2) is the singular of the same word. |

| ventiláre (cornu) | lançar ao ar (*com o chifre, lançaremos ao ar os nossos inimigos*) | open | Ps 43:6 (κερατιοῦμεν); L&S 'toss in the air, winnow'. Options *sacudir*, *derrubar* (DRB; supplantáre's). The stylist moved *com o chifre* forward (v2). |
| diripere | saquear (*saqueavam para si*) | open | Ps 43:11; 88:42 *diripuérunt eum omnes transeúntes* (grep) should follow. |
| commutátio | troca (*nas trocas deles*) | open | Ps 43:13; 88:52 *commutatiónem Christi tui* is another sense (grep) and will want its own look. |

| obloqui | insultar (*do que me afronta e do que me insulta*) | open | Ps 43:17 (παραλαλέω; L&S cites this verse); once in the psalter. *difamar* is detráhere's (D41), *censura* vituperátio's. Two persons (article repeated, v2, the Latinist); the supplied *me* held as grammar against him (twice, minor). |

| verecúndia | desonra (*a minha desonra está diante de mim*) | open | Ps 43:16 (ἐντροπή, the Greek of reveréntia at 34:26b → *desonra*); confúsio beside it → *vergonha* (D41). 68:8, 68:20 (grep) should follow. |

| similitúdo (παραβολή, a byword) | termo de comparação (*Fizestes de nós um termo de comparação para as nações*) | open | Ps 43:15 (v2, the stylist; draft 1 *uma comparação*). The Latinist at the gate called it paraphrase and asked *semelhança* (minor, refused: no sentence in Portuguese). 68:12 *factus sum illis in parábolam* is another word. |

| commótio cápitis | um abanar de cabeça | open | Ps 43:15 (v2; draft 1 *meneio*, unknown to the blind reader); *abanar a cabeça* is the sideways shake, not the nod. 21:8 *movérunt caput* is movére (*moveram a cabeça*). |

| conglutináre | colar (*o nosso ventre está colado à terra*) | open | Ps 43:25 (ἐκολλήθη, the Greek of adhærére at 21:16 *colou-se*); once in the psalter. The Sexagesima Introit quotes it with *adhǽsit*. |

| post (after avértere retrórsum) | após (*Fizestes-nos voltar para trás após os nossos inimigos*) | open | Ps 43:11 (v2, the Latinist: draft 1 *diante dos* followed the Greek παρά). *atrás dos* stacks with *para trás*. |

| operári (opus) | operar (*a obra que operastes*) | open | Ps 43:2b; the noun-verb echo of the Latin and Greek. *operastes* was unknown to the blind reader; option *fizestes*. *operári iniquitátem → praticar* is untouched. 73:12 *operátus est salútem*, 89:16–17 *ópera … opus mánuum* (grep) will meet it. |
| æstimári | ser tido (*fomos tidos como ovelhas de matança*) | open | Ps 43:22b (= Rom 8:36; v2, the stylist; draft 1 *considerados*). 87:5 *æstimátus sum* (grep) should follow. |
| possidére | possuir (*não possuíram a terra*) | open | Ps 43:4; many verses (24:13, 36:9 …, grep) — check their renderings before settling. |
